page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a memory-allocated virtual machine instance from the n1 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 13.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 6.5 GB per vCPU. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and includes a 45 MB L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this configuration, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-highmem-2 in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1105.58, which is in the bottom 25%, while the multi-core score of 1452.88 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 80.89 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 11.13 GB/sec, both categorized in the bottom 10%. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 944.0 and a multi-core score of 1124.0. Database operations via Passmark register at 603.54, and Redis SET operations achieve 1.38 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-2 offers an entry-level option for workloads requiring more memory than standard general-purpose instances without scaling up vCPU count. However, there is a clear trade-off, as compute and memory bandwidth performance are relatively weak. This instance is best suited for low-intensity workloads that are memory-bound rather than compute-bound, such as small databases, basic caching layers, lightweight web serving, or simple background workers.
